leads.name: Sprookjesboom
leads.status: BLOCKED 2026-09-06: not a living tree, so it fails the alive-entry requirement (hard rule: never doe aan dode bomen / no dead-or-non-living entries; also a fabrication risk under hard rule 2 if presented as a real specimen). Verified via Eftepedia (the detailed Efteling fan reference, cross-checked against English Wikipedia's 'Sprookjesboom' article and general web search): the Sprookjesboom in the Efteling's Sprookjesbos (Fairytale Forest, opened 1 April 2010) is an entirely artificial audio-animatronic structure, 9m tall and 9-13m wide, built on an 8-tonne internal steel framework with roughly 50,000 artificial leaves and 1,500 fabricated branch ends, built in-house by Efteling with external specialists Jora Vision and P&P Projects. A real tree's bark was used only as a mould reference for texturing the fake bark (same technique as the park's separate Trollenkoning prop); no living wood or root system is part of the structure. Note for future passes: do not confuse this with Kniesoor, a DIFFERENT attraction elsewhere in the same park where the trunk IS a real living tree with only an animatronic face and mouth added to it; Kniesoor would need its own separate verification if ever proposed as a candidate, since a real tree wearing a prop face is a different case from a wholly fabricated structure. Never ship the Sprookjesboom as a collectible tree entry.
